description: We are a group of students searching to innovate in the sanitary field in space.
summary:
Panacea is a mobile application designed to monitor and evaluate the physical, cognitive and emotional health states of astronauts during space missions. This development combines different measurements from various tests or different devices, thus obtaining a broad view of the astronauts' states.

This challenge addresses the maintenance or improvement of the astronaut's condition, and through the parameters of physical tests, through evaluations based on neurocognitive tests (memory, reaction, attention, coordination). By comparing reference values and personal parameters, possible dangers and drastic changes can be identified.

This project is important, since astronauts are exposed to changes due to variations in states that one site or another presents, affecting their physical and cognitive state. Therefore, monitoring is essential for identifying possible risks and acting against these possible risks, especially in long space missions.
details:
WHAT IT DOES?

Panacea is a mobile application that consists of monitoring the physical state, cognitive state and emotional state. To do this, different types of tests and evaluations are carried out, and they are even combined, allowing the parameters of the astronaut's well-being to be visualized in a general way.



HOW IT WORKS?

Panacea works as follows in the different sections:

Physiological monitoring

By means of measured parameters, these are compared with reference ranges and usual values. In this way, possible risks can be identified and detected, issuing these possible risks to both the astronaut and the doctor.

In this part, it focuses on jugular venous thrombosis, hemodynamic alterations (evolution of heart rate and blood pressure) and cardiorespiratory alterations.

For example, in jugular venous thrombosis, if there is dyspnea, chest pain, syncope, or other symptoms, it means that it is an emergency, and therefore, an alert would appear (to the doctor and the astronaut).



Neurocognitive evaluation

Previously, on Earth, neurocognitive tests, STROOP (selective attention and inhibitory control), N-Back (working memory) and PVT (Psychomotor Vigilance test) are performed. These results obtained on Earth will serve to obtain a reference.

Once in space, tests are carried out periodically, and the results obtained are compared both with the reference data (those from Earth) and with the results obtained in space. In this way, different changes in cognitive performance can be identified. For example, if there is an increase in reaction time in the PVT, a decrease in hits or a greater number of errors in N-Back, an increase in response time, among others, it could indicate a possible worsening in certain cognitive abilities.

With these cognitive follow-ups, the evolution of the astronaut can be observed, deviations from their reference values can be detected, and possible warning signs related to sleep disturbance or the conditions of the space mission (gravity, isolation, fatigue, etc.) can be identified.

Emotional well-being

Mood, stress, and isolation are monitored daily, with suggestions based on the responses.

There is also the “box breathing” technique (4-4-4-4). Additionally, there is a memory mini-game called “Orbital Pairs,” ideas for feeling close to loved ones, and a “Talk to a Counselor” button that notifies the doctor.


Other functions/sections:

In addition to this, 2 profiles are included, the astronaut profile and the doctor profile:

ASTRONAUT PROFILE

Some of the various sections of the astronaut profile are:

  • Daily record with habits (optional). Food consumed, liquids ingested and the type and time of exercise carried out the previous day. If you have not filled in this section, it will appear "No data".
    • Daily monitoring of mood, stress and isolation, supplemented by suggestions based on the answers obtained.
    • Data: number of crew members are on alert, in a state of surveillance and in normal status. Warnings and protocols.
    • Each crew member appears with their respective profiles, ordered according to the state of emergency. Each crew member profile contains their corresponding general statuses, cognitive tests, protocols, warnings/alerts and small graphs. These small graphs cover the constant 7-day measurements.
    • The doctor can also enter constants of any astronaut from his profile.

PHYSICIAN PROFILE

  • Mission. This part contains the day of the mission, the delay with the Earth and updates with the hours of the last data received.
  • Data: number of crew members are on alert, in a state of surveillance and in normal status. Warnings and protocols.
  • Each crew member appears with their respective profiles, ordered according to the state of emergency. Each crew member profile contains their corresponding general statuses, cognitive tests, protocols, warnings/alerts and small graphs. These small graphs cover the constant 7-day measurements.

These are some of the many sections to highlight.



BENEFITS  

This project offers a comprehensive solution for health monitoring, bringing together all the information about an astronaut's physiological, cognitive, and emotional state in a single application. One of the key benefits is the ability to quickly or early detect personalized changes, alterations, and deviations from each astronaut's reference/normal values. The alerts issued in response to potential risk alerts also facilitate communication between the astronaut and medical personnel, leading to better supervision.

IMPACT

The desired impact is to help improve the confidence, safety, and well-being of astronauts before, during, and after missions. With these commented follow-ups, both the astronaut and the doctor can easily stay in contact, without high concern for symptoms thanks to those alerts.

This project focuses more on obtaining personalized assessments, allowing the doctor to make a more tailored decision. Additionally, it aims to contribute to the development of future space missions in a safer and easier manner, especially for long-duration missions.

CREATIVITY

This project is creative because it is something useful but also with a logic behind all this. From individual profiles, personalized follow-ups, alerts, protocols, graphs, to existing neurocognitive tests studied by experts, tests such as STROOP.

Not only that, but this mobile application works without the Earth, being able to make urgent decisions on board, that is, on the spot. In addition, the reason for each warning appears. In turn, all the astronaut's data (sleep, habits, mood, attention tests, memory, etc.) appear in one place, which is the application.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

For the factors, we have considered the possible decreases or increases, in the different parts (Earth, space, Moon,...) in which the astronauts are going to find themselves.

We have also used the real-world datasets from the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) and the SpaceX Inspiration4 mission (September 2021, 3 days in orbit with a civilian crew) as reference data. Each dataset is stored as a CSV file within the app, so it works offline.

For Blood Count: LSDS-7

  • We have used the LSDS-7_Complete_Blood_Count_CBC_TRANSFORMED.csv file
  • It contains the blood samples of the 4 crew members at 7 times: before the flight and after the return.
  • It also contains 20 parameters (hemoglobin, leukocytes, platelets, etc.), each parameter with its reference range.

For Biochemistry (Metabolic Panel): LSDS-8/ OSD-575

  • We have used the LSDS-8_Comprehensive_Methabolic_Panel_CMP_TRANSFORMED.csv file
  • What it contains are the serum samples of the 4 crew members and the 7 moments (the blood count). It also contains 17 parameters (urea, creatinine, potassium, bicarbonate, glucose, calcium, etc.) Everything else in the demo is simulated, not NASA data.

There is additional information compiled from research and reports by NASA. And other parts of the demo are simulated.

TOOLS USED

The tools used for this project were:

  • Claude: As a programming and information resource.
  • Java: Used for programming.
  • GitHub: As a repository for storing, managing, and collaborating on all source code as a team.
  • Android Studio: As the application development environment.
  • Kotlin: As an alternative programming language.
  • Cambridge Dictionary: For languages
